deep_dive.title: Learning to Discriminate Scene Structures Makes Self-Supervised Depth Learning Scalable
deep_dive.abstract: Self-supervised monocular depth estimation is appealing for its potential to scale with unlabeled data, yet existing methods often degrade when trained on diverse scenes. This study finds that, under self-supervision, models tend to encode dataset-specific structural biases rather than transferable scene geometry, leading to cross-domain optimization conflicts. To address this issue, this study proposes the MaSS framework, aiming to make self-supervised depth learning scalable to diverse data. MaSS introduces a dedicated structural representation pathway explicitly decoupled from contextual features, which is guided by a novel scene-structure discrimination objective to learn generalized, layout-aware structural representations for depth decoding. Trained and evaluated on four diverse datasets, both individually and jointly, MaSS substantially outperforms prior self-supervised methods and is the first to consistently benefit from mixed-domain training. Zero-shot evaluation on eight additional datasets further demonstrates its remarkable generalizability, particularly on those entirely out-of-distribution scenes. The source code is publicly available at https://mias.group/MaSS.

deep_dive.title: FlashReFocus: Interactive Image Refocusing in Seconds
deep_dive.abstract: Single-image refocusing changes the focal plane and depth of field of a photograph after capture. It is inherently interactive: users try many focal points and blur strengths on one image, so each edit should be fast and change only the blur. Recent generative methods, however, rerun large diffusion models for every edit. We observe that the two sub-problems differ in kind: recovering the all-in-focus image is ill-posed and needs a generative prior, whereas rendering blur is largely determined by depth and the focal plane. We therefore propose FlashReFocus, which runs diffusion once per photograph and renders every edit with a lightweight network. To address the ill-posed restoration, a one-step diffusion deblurrer with a decoder refiner recovers fine detail efficiently while balancing fidelity and perceptual quality. For precise control, the renderer is conditioned on an explicit defocus map and uses defocus-bias attention, which lets pixels at similar defocus share information without interference from pixels at other depths; in-focus content stays unchanged, and editing the map yields tilt-shift and two focal planes. To further test generalization to unseen cameras, we collect 3CReal, a three-camera benchmark of 89 pairs. FlashReFocus achieves the best perceptual fidelity for zero-shot bokeh rendering on EBB! and 3CReal, refocuses 148.3x faster than GenRefocus, and takes about half a second per further edit, 462x faster.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_en: FlashReFocus separates single-image refocusing into all-in-focus restoration and blur rendering, running diffusion once and applying a lightweight depth-and-focal-plane network for each edit, enabling fast interactive depth-of-field control.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 单图重聚焦需要在拍摄后改变焦平面和景深，且用户会反复尝试不同焦点与虚化强度，而现有生成式方法每次编辑都需重跑大型扩散模型，速度慢。本文提出FlashReFocus，将问题拆为两部分：用一步扩散去模糊器加解码细化器恢复全清晰图像，而模糊渲染则交给由深度和焦平面决定的轻量网络完成。这样每张照片只需运行一次扩散，之后每次编辑都快速生成且只改变模糊。该工作为交互式景深渲染与神经虚化提供了高效范式。

quick_skim.title: MaskMerge: Structure-aware Token Merging for Efficient Instance Segmentation
quick_skim.abstract: Token merging improves the efficiency of Vision Transformers by combining redundant tokens, but existing methods largely rely on feature similarity to determine which tokens to merge. This criterion is effective for semantic segmentation, yet can fail in instance segmentation, where adjacent objects of the same class often have highly similar features. We identify this failure mode as cross-instance token fusion. We introduce MaskMerge, an instance-aware token merging method that uses coarse intermediate mask predictions to constrain feature-based merging and preserve instance boundaries. We evaluate MaskMerge on two diverse instance segmentation domains characterized by high inter-instance visual similarity: PanNuke and iSAID. Against the SOTA token merging method ALGM, MaskMerge improves mAP from 30.1 to 32.1 on PanNuke while reducing computation from 229 to 153 GFLOPs and running 1.18x faster, and from 33.1 to 36.2 on iSAID while reducing computation from 198 to 182 GFLOPs and running 1.23x faster. Additionally, we also test it on Cityscapes and match ALGM's performance while using fewer FLOPs. The gains also transfer to an MAE pretrained backbone, demonstrating that instance-aware merging enables more aggressive compression when appearance similarity alone cannot reliably preserve object identity.
quick_skim.llm_evidence_en: instance-aware token merging preserving instance boundaries in instance segmentation
quick_skim.llm_evidence_cn: 实例感知令牌合并，在实例分割中保留实例边界

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: MaskMerge constrains ViT token merging with coarse mask predictions to prevent cross-instance fusion, improving efficiency and boundary preservation in instance segmentation.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 视觉Transformer的令牌合并多依据特征相似度，但在实例分割中同类相邻物体特征相近，容易发生跨实例令牌融合而破坏边界。本文提出MaskMerge，利用粗略的中间掩码预测约束基于特征的合并过程，从而保留实例边界并维持效率。在PanNuke与iSAID这两个高实例相似度数据集上，该方法优于当前先进的令牌合并方案，说明引入掩码结构先验可让高效令牌合并在实例分割中兼顾精度与边界完整性。
